You have unlocked a handful of powers—fragments of insight that grant you an enduring connection to the Force. General forcecasting rules appear in chapter 10, and the list of force powers in chapter 11.

Force Powers Known. You start knowing 4 force powers of your choice, learning more as you level up, per the Force Powers Known column of the Aing-Tii Order Forcecasting table. You cannot learn a power whose level exceeds your Max Power Level, though you may learn a power alongside its prerequisite at the same time.

Force Points. Your pool of force points, used to fuel your powers, equals your monk level (per the Force Points column of the table) plus your Wisdom or Charisma modifier, whichever you choose. You regain every spent point after a long rest.

Max Power Level. Certain powers can be overpowered by spending additional force points for a stronger effect; the highest level you can overpower to rises as you gain levels, per the Max Power Level column of the table. You may cast a power at 4th level only once between long rests, regaining the ability to do so after resting.

Forcecasting Ability. Which ability governs your powers depends on their alignment: Wisdom for light-side powers, Charisma for dark-side powers, and either (your choice) for universal powers. Use whichever ability applies whenever a power calls for your forcecasting ability, including when setting its save DC or making an attack roll with it.

Force save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your forcecasting ability modifier

Force attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your forcecasting ability modifier
